transactions.what: Claim link minted: 2 STRK withdrawn from the pool into LumenEscrow behind a Poseidon commitment. Claimable by whoever holds the secret, with no wallet or pool registration needed until they open it.

LumenEscrow deployed with claim_to_address — the second door. A claim can now be collected straight to a public address by someone who has never joined the privacy pool, has no shielded balance, and cannot pay the pool's flat fee.

Claim relayed to a wallet that had never joined the privacy pool, held no shielded balance, had no gas, and whose account contract was not deployed — and still is not. The recipient performed no action. A third party submitted claim_to_address; the Poseidon preimage was the only authority.

Claim link minted for 9.845994 STRK. The amount was tuned away from a round 10 by the guard, because the escrowed amount is public and a round number is the easiest thing to match a later withdrawal against.

The same link collected through the private door: the pool credits an open note, so the arrival is shielded and nothing about the recipient is published. Compare with 0x3af9f5cd, which is the public door — one link shape, two landings.

Three people paid in one operation via DepositMany: 2.8 STRK split into 0.933333 STRK links, three Deposited events and one BatchDeposited under a single pool fee. Sequentially the same payout costs the flat fee three times, so batching is a 3x cost argument here and a 50x one for an agent paying a payroll — and an observer sees one operation, not three.

A link nobody collected, reclaimed by its sender after the refund window opened — and out of a superseded escrow, since the entry was minted before the current one was deployed. Claim and refund secrets hash under separate domains, so the reclaim key can never spend a link and the link can never trigger a reclaim. Money parked behind a secret cannot be stranded by a recipient who never shows up.
